title: PRD: Indexed Multi-Intent Endpoint Bundle & Launch Safety Checklist
creator: Asha Kapoor
summary: Deliver a single, documented hosted API bundle that supports multi-intent requests combining generation (chat/completions), sparse/dense embeddings, and reranking in a single logical endpoint. The bundle prioritizes low-latency intent-aware routing, index-preserving embedding options, and deterministic fallbacks for capacity degradation.
background: Customers building conversational assistants and retrieval-augmented generation ask for a single API surface that can accept mixed intents (generate + embed + rerank) with consistent behavioral contracts across lanes. Existing hosted endpoints handle each capability separately which increases client complexity and cross-call latency. This PRD defines an "Indexed Multi-Intent Endpoint Bundle" to reduce client chattiness, improve end-to-end p95 latency for RAG flows, and provide operational guarantees for launch.
goals: Provide a single, documented bundle endpoint that accepts a structured request mixing generation, embedding, and rerank steps
Ensure behavioral determinism for generation profiles used in bundle requests (seed control, temperature mapping, token limits)
Keep end-to-end p95 user-perceived latency for a typical 3-step RAG bundle (query->embed->rerank->generate) under 800ms in hosted Tier-1 regions
Ship SDK updates and migration guide for customers to adopt the bundle without runtime changes
Provide robust fallbacks (model variant and lane-level degrade) that preserve semantic guarantees when capacity is constrained
non_goals: Do not redesign the existing model catalog or add new models beyond verified variants
Do not change billing primitives (per-token/per-embedding unit) at launch; cost transparency is required but pricing change is out of scope
No initial support for multimodal inputs (images/audio) in this launch
user_stories: As a product engineer, I want to call one endpoint to get embeddings for retrieval, rerank candidates, and produce a final assistant response so I can reduce client-side orchestration
As an SRE, I want deterministic degrade behavior that falls back to a lower-cost model variant without changing response schema so client retries are minimized
As a compliance owner, I want tenant isolation and KMS integration available for Private/Dedicated customers using this bundle
api_contract: Request schema: JSON with top-level 'steps' array. Each step has 'type' in {embed, rerank, generate} and a 'mode' (sync|async).

Response schema: 'bundle_id', 'steps_result' array preserving step order, normalized temperature and token fields for generate step, canonical embedding arrays for embed step, confidence scores for rerank step
Behavioral guarantee: step outputs for identical inputs must be stable for the pinned model version in the release window
Streaming: support streaming for final generate step via same chunked streaming semantics as existing chat endpoint
Error model: per-step error codes and global bundle-level 'partial_result' boolean to allow best-effort responses
performance_targets: p50 end-to-end (single-region warm cache) < 220ms for simple embed-only bundles
p95 end-to-end (3-step typical RAG) < 800ms for hosted Tier-1 regions
Tail latency degradation policy: if p99 breaches 2x baseline for 5m, automatically route new requests to low-cost variant and emit rollout event
Throughput target: sustain 2x expected initial qps for canary traffic slice without OOMs
acceptance_criteria: API contract documented and validated by SDK integration tests
E2E synthetic workload (RAG mix) passes p95 and p50 performance targets in staging under realistic traffic profile
Canary slice (1% of production) runs 48h with no more than 5% error rate increase compared to baseline and no regression in quality metrics
Quality regression gates: automatically reject release if generation BLEU/ROUGE equivalent or embedding similarity for a set of 200 probes drops more than 3% relative to control
Operator playbook completed and runbook linked in console under 'Deployments -> Bundles'
SDK clients for Python/TS updated and published with migration snippets and three sample apps
Documentation: OpenAPI spec, quickstart guide, and a migration FAQ published
Security: design reviewed and security checklist signed off including KMS integration for Private customers and audit log hooks
Billing: cost-estimation dashboard available and per-token/per-embed accounting visible in console
launch_checklist: Finalize API surface and publish OpenAPI and example curl/SDK snippets
Merge SDK changes and publish packages (python redwood-infer-bundles, @redwood/sdk-bundles)
Complete canary config: feature-flag gate, 1% routing, and auto-rollback hook
Run full acceptance test-suite in staging (integration + performance + chaos) and record artifacts
Compose operator runbook and link relevant dashboards (latency, errors, token cost) in console
Complete cost model review and publish expected unit-cost guidance for customers
Stakeholder review: Product, Engineering, Docs, SRE, Security sign-off
Set up migration communication: email template, changelog entry, and sample migration guide
Enable telemetry events for bundle usage and extract per-step token/bandwidth metrics
Prepare post-launch monitoring dashboard and alert thresholds (p95, error rate, quality drift)
telemetry_and_sla: Emit per-bundle and per-step metrics: request_count, success_count, error_count, p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens_consumed
Quality signals: embedding similarity distribution vs baseline, rerank accuracy on probe set, generation perplexity buckets
SLO targets: 99.7% availability for bundle API in hosted Tier-1 regions; latency SLO for p95 as defined in performance_targets
Retention: telemetry retained for 90 days in console for rollout evaluation
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal alpha (eng + SE teams) for two weeks - flagged, no external traffic
Phase 1: limited beta (select customers) - 1% traffic, manual monitoring and weekly sync
Phase 2: broad canary - 10% traffic for 72 hours with automated gating
Phase 3: general availability - 100% traffic, announce migration tools and sample app
Rollback criteria: sustained p95 > 2x baseline for 10m OR quality gate failure OR > 5% user-visible error-rate increase
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Increased client-side confusion around step ordering -> Mitigation: Provide clear examples, validation on server-side, and strong SDK helpers that enforce schema
Risk: Higher tail-latency when embedding indexes cold -> Mitigation: pre-warm common index prefixes in canary, soft-start traffic shaping
Risk: Cost surprises for heavy embedding customers -> Mitigation: cost-estimation page, opt-in index-preserving mode (lower dimension/quantized embeddings) and quota defaults
Risk: Security and tenant isolation gaps for Private/Dedicated customers -> Mitigation: require KMS binding in Private by default for first wave and add audit hooks before GA
notes: This proposal focuses on a pragmatic first release: stable behavioral contracts, clear acceptance gates, and operational runbooks. Subsequent releases may expand multimodal inputs and richer indexed retrieval connectors. Keep acceptance gates strict to avoid user-visible quality regressions. If early telemetry shows unexpected cost patterns, pause rollouts and enable lower-dimension quantized embeddings as a mitigation.
